**Void Deck now brings its own startup movie.** The boot video is the one moment the interface is still dark, so it
belongs to the theme too: the CtOS sequence from *Watchdogs* — dots folding into shapes, a retro loading bar, and
the hexagon logo. It is 1280×800, eight seconds, silent, and one switch in the Quick Access panel installs it. A
movie you had before is set aside rather than overwritten, and switching the feature off puts yours straight back.

**The video is the fan-made [Watchdogs Boot Animation](https://github.com/ShorterKing/Watchdogs-Boot-Animation) by
Akshat Singh** (GPL-3.0), converted from the Android flashable package into a Deck-sized WebM. The portrait frames
are cropped to 16:10 without stretching them, the logo lands in the exact centre of the screen, and the sequence
gets a short hold at the end so the last frame is not a flash. The credit and the exact conversion steps are in
[`third_party/CTOS-BOOT-ANIMATION.md`](https://github.com/endoflineservice/VoidDeck/blob/main/third_party/CTOS-BOOT-ANIMATION.md).

**And the lock screen finally joins the theme.** The PIN entry screen is void black like the rest of Steam: square
PIN cells, a three-column pad of square keys, dot-matrix numerals, and the focused key inverted to solid ink so you
always know where you are typing.

**Two Steam oddities are gone.** The tabs on a game's details page no longer keep Steam's own white pill, so the
label and the background can no longer end up white on white; they are cut and framed like the rest of the theme
now. And Steam's settings no longer sneaks a blue bar into the otherwise black and white sidebar: the category
you are in is marked with the same thin ink rule the rest of Void Deck uses.

**Install / update:** grab `VoidDeck-v1.5.0.zip` from the [v1.5.0 release](https://github.com/endoflineservice/VoidDeck/releases/tag/v1.5.0), or press **Update now** in the Void Deck panel.
